# Model specification: dma-controller 1.0.0

Stream/channel DMA controller (and request multiplexer) as used by PX4 and ArduPilot for UART, SPI, I2C, SDMMC and ADC transfers.

## Features

| Feature | Meaning |
|---|---|
| base | Streams with addresses, counts, widths, increments, circular mode, HT/TC/TE. |
| fifo | FIFO mode and width conversion. |
| double_buffer | Double-buffer memory side. |
| mux | Requests routed through a request multiplexer (DMAMUX) instead of fixed channel numbers. |

## Terms

| Term | Kind | Feature | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| stream_enable | control | base | The stream accepts requests; clearing it stops the stream. |
| direction | control | base | Peripheral-to-memory, memory-to-peripheral or memory-to-memory. |
| request_select | control | base | Which peripheral request drives the stream (channel number, or the multiplexer's request id). |
| peripheral_address | control | base | Address on the peripheral side. |
| memory_address | control | base | Address on the memory side (and second buffer with double_buffer). |
| item_count | control | base | Items left; decremented per item, reloaded in circular mode. |
| peripheral_width | control | base | Item size on the peripheral side (8/16/32). |
| memory_width | control | base | Item size on the memory side. |
| peripheral_increment | control | base | Peripheral address advances per item. |
| memory_increment | control | base | Memory address advances per item. |
| circular | control | base | item_count and addresses reload after the last item. |
| half_transfer | status | base | Half of the items moved. |
| transfer_complete | status | base | All items moved. |
| transfer_error | status | base | Access to an address with no memory or device. |
| flag_ack | ack | base | Clears the stream's flags (write 1 to clear). |
| ht_irq_enable | control | base | half_transfer raises the stream irq. |
| tc_irq_enable | control | base | transfer_complete raises the stream irq. |
| te_irq_enable | control | base | transfer_error raises the stream irq. |
| stream_irq | event | base | One interrupt line per stream (Devicetree interrupts, in stream order). |
| fifo_mode | control | fifo | Direct mode or FIFO mode with threshold; needed for width conversion. |
| double_buffer | control | double_buffer | Memory side alternates between two buffers. |
| current_target | status | double_buffer | Which of the two buffers is in use. |
| mux_request_id | control | mux | Request multiplexer: peripheral request id routed to the stream's channel. |

## Behaviour rules

| Rule | Feature | Rule text |
|---|---|---|
| ADV-DMA-B001 | base | While stream_enable is on, each request from the selected peripheral moves one item between the two addresses in direction, and item_count decreases by one (ADV-DMA-001); requests from other peripherals are ignored. |
| ADV-DMA-B002 | mux | With the multiplexer, only requests whose id equals mux_request_id of the stream's channel reach the stream. |
| ADV-DMA-B003 | base | half_transfer turns on when item_count reaches half, transfer_complete when it reaches 0, each at the clock of that item (ADV-DMA-002); without circular the stream then turns stream_enable off. |
| ADV-DMA-B004 | base | With circular, after the last item item_count and addresses reload and the stream continues (ADV-DMA-003). |
| ADV-DMA-B005 | fifo | With different peripheral and memory widths, items are packed and unpacked as the reference manual's width table states (ADV-DMA-004). |
| ADV-DMA-B006 | base | An access to an address with no memory or device sets transfer_error and turns the stream off. |
| ADV-DMA-B007 | base | stream_irq is raised while (ht_irq_enable and half_transfer) or (tc_irq_enable and transfer_complete) or (te_irq_enable and transfer_error); flag_ack clears the acknowledged flags. |
| ADV-DMA-B008 | double_buffer | With double_buffer, after each complete pass the memory side switches buffers and current_target changes. |
| ADV-DMA-B009 | base | Configuration changes to addresses, count, widths or direction while stream_enable is on are ignored, as the manuals require the stream to be off. |

**Timing.** Each item completes at the clock of the request that caused it; the timing rules of docs/device-tree-design.md apply.

**Out of scope.** bus arbitration and stream priority timing, burst transfers (stored only), peripheral flow control, MDMA, request generators of the multiplexer, synchronization inputs
